extracted.intended_audience: general audience interested in entertainment/celebrity news
extracted.subtask_description: A news listicle summarizing major controversial actions by comedian Roseanne Barr, describing incidents, public reactions, and her explanations or recantations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The tweets from Roseanne Barr that led to the cancellation of her hit ABC series
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes that a series of tweets Barr sent (including one about former Obama administration official Valerie Jarrett: "Muslim brotherhood & planet of the apes had a baby=vj.") led ABC to axe the 'Roseanne' reboot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This incident is presented as the most recent controversy and an example of how incendiary social-media posts can have immediate professional consequences (cancellation by the network).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Star-Spangled Banner' performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Barr turned in what is now considered one of the all-time worst 'Star-Spangled Banner' performances when she sang at a 1990 San Diego Padres game: audible boos, shrieking, at one point putting a finger in her ears; concluded with a crotch grab and spitting on the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The performance was roundly condemned (President George H.W. Bush called it "disgraceful"). At a press conference Barr explained she was "simply trying to be funny," saying, "None of this was meant viciously... Nobody feels worse than me." This item illustrates public performance choices that provoke backlash and the standard of public condemnation that can follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recanting sex abuse claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Barr shocked fans in 1991 when she claimed she had been sexually abused as a child ('My name is Roseanne and I am an incest survivor'). In 2011 she recanted on Oprah Winfrey, calling it "the worst thing I’ve ever done. It’s the biggest mistake that I’ve ever made."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Her later explanation blamed psychiatric drugs and mental illness: she described being prescribed numerous psychiatric drugs and losing touch with reality. This item highlights the gravity of public claims and the reputational impact of recantations/explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing as Hitler
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2009, Barr posed for Heeb magazine dressed as Adolf Hitler pulling burned cookies in the shape of people from an oven; Barr — who is Jewish — requested the look. The photos resurfaced after the 'Roseanne' reboot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: She attempted to explain her motivation in a 2011 interview, insisting she was not trying to make fun of Jewish people or the Holocaust and offering a rationale about overuse of Holocaust references: "There’s another, deeper layer to it... it’s so f***ing every day now, Holocaust, it’s like baking cookies." This illustrates use of provocative imagery and subsequent public explanation/defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing address of George Zimmerman’s parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortly after Trayvon Martin was killed, Barr retweeted the home address of Zimmerman’s parents and wrote, 'If Zimmerman isn’t arrested I’ll rt his address again — maybe go 2 his house myself,' a tweet that was later deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robert and Gladys Zimmerman sued Barr in 2014, saying her actions caused them to go into hiding; the suit was thrown out in 2015. This example highlights actions that endanger individuals and lead to legal consequences or public condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern: often offered explanations once backlash erupts
rubrics_metrics.description: The story highlights that Barr 'is no stranger to controversy' and that 'She's often offered explanations once backlash erupts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the examples, Barr responds to backlash with explanations, apologies, or recantations (e.g., claiming she was trying to be funny after the anthem, recanting abuse claims, explaining the Heeb shoot). This functions as an implicit evaluative dimension: whether the subject provides explanations and how those explanations affect public perception.
